newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond spreads mixed despite rally.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond spreads mixed despite rally.

text.p: Australian bond spreads ended mixed despite a rally in the local market, with long bonds the best performer on the day after a solid rally in U.S. Treasuries overnight.
The long end strength saw the curve flatten slightly, reversing the trend seen earlier this week.

Traders said with the short end having almost fully factored in a first quarter rate cut, its potential to rally further may be limited and so the curve may have a bias to flatten if the market continues to rally.

While spreads finished mixed, there was still good demand for local assets. Traders said the improved inflation outlook was compensating investors for the prospect of potentially lower nominal interest rates.
"There's still good demand out there for Australian paper, and that probably explains some of the spread contraction that we are seeing," one trader said.
Others felt that with the spread to the U.S. 10-year bond narrowing to around 90 points, some of that demand may thin and see the curve settle between 90 and 100 points.

"There's been a little bit of interest and people switching into Aussie and New Zealand out of Canada and Europe and Treasuries ... but I think they are getting down to levels where the interest is probably going not to be as strong as what it has been," a trader at a European investment house said.
